name: Dermablend / tattoo cover

lead: Dermablend is a brand of high-coverage camouflage makeup, and tattoo cover products like it hide tattoos, scars, birthmarks, vitiligo patches and bruises on the face or body. The concealing effect shows as soon as it is applied.

Wikipedia describes cosmetic camouflage as creams or powders that hide color or texture irregularities, first developed by plastic surgeons in World War II for burns, and says it may reduce the psychological impact of skin imperfections. No published trials of specific products were found.

paras: Opaque, pigment-rich cream or powder is applied over the area to match the surrounding skin tone, often with color-correcting shades such as green to neutralise redness. It lasts until washed off and is reapplied as needed.
As with other cosmetics, ingredients can cause irritation or allergic reactions in some people. The makeup wears off and needs reapplication.

angle.text: Camouflage makeup such as Dermablend covers tattoos, scars, vitiligo patches and bruises with heavier coverage than foundation, so skin looks even from the moment it is applied. It lasts until it is washed off.

lead: Dermablend is a brand of high-coverage camouflage makeup, and tattoo cover refers to opaque concealers of this type used to hide tattoos, scars, birthmarks, vitiligo, redness and other discoloration on the face or body. People use them to present clearer, more even-looking skin or to leave a tattoo unseen for a photo, job or event.[1]

Cosmetic camouflage, also called cover or corrective makeup, uses creams or powders to conceal color or texture irregularities. Wikipedia says the first camouflage creams were developed by plastic surgeons during World War II to cover severe burns on fighter pilots, and that men, women and children now use them.[1]

Dermablend has been used in published dermatology studies. A study of 73 women with facial pigmentary disorders reported improved Skindex-16 quality-of-life scores that continued through three months, and a 30-patient program tested a Dermablend concealer on post-procedure bruising.[2][3]

paras: Cosmetic camouflage refers to creams or powders that hide color or texture irregularities, and covers angiomas, redness, telangiectasia, vitiligo, sunspots, acne, burns, stretch marks, scars, bruises, rosacea and tattoos. Wikipedia adds that it may reduce the psychological impact of skin imperfections.[1]
For redness, Wikipedia's article describes using a green concealer sparingly to neutralize the color.[1]
According to Wikipedia, the first camouflage creams were developed by plastic surgeons during World War II for burns on fighter pilots.[1]

sections.h: Use for tattoos and skin concealment
paras: Tattoo cover products are layered to match the surrounding skin tone over inked areas. Because the makeup sits on the surface, the tattoo itself is unchanged and the cover can be removed at the end of the day.[1]

A study of 73 women with severe facial pigmentary disorders, including acne, hypopigmentation, lentigines, melasma, rosacea, vascular proliferations and scars, applied Dermablend corrective cosmetic and assessed 63 with the Skindex-16. Scores improved and the improvement continued, reaching 30 percent at three months, and the product was well tolerated.[2]

A user experience program in 30 women with post-procedural bruising tested Dermablend Professional Cover Care Full Coverage Concealer. Users needed on average 1.55 coats; 78.18 percent displayed clear skin with no erythema and 21.82 percent almost clear skin with slight redness, and no physician-reported adverse events related to the product were reported.[3]

timeline.event: Plastic surgeons develop the first camouflage creams for burned fighter pilots.[1]
Cutis study reports quality-of-life improvement in women using Dermablend for facial pigmentary disorders.[2]
Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology reports a Dermablend concealer program for post-procedural bruising.[3]
